Lesson 04: Exploring Simple Circuits (Grade 3, Explore Phase, 5E Model)

Learning Objective: Students will construct simple circuits and identify the conditions needed to
light a bulb.

Performance Expectation: 4-PS3-2. Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be
transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
DCI: PS3.B — Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
Focal SEP: Constructing Explanations and Designing Solutions
Focal CCC: Energy and Matter

Timing: 45 minutes

Student-Facing Sequence:
1. Hook (5 min): Students examine a disassembled flashlight and discuss with a partner what parts
   they think are needed to make the bulb light up.
2. Materials Exploration (10 min): Each group receives a battery, a bulb, and two wires, and is
   challenged to light the bulb using trial and error.
3. Structured Circuit Building (15 min): Following a diagram, students build a complete circuit and
   record which configurations worked and which did not in a simple chart (works / doesn't work).
4. Variation Challenge (10 min): Groups try adding a switch or a second bulb and record what changes.
5. Wrap-Up Discussion (5 min): Whole-class share-out: one group at a time explains what made their
   circuit work.

Teacher Notes: Some groups may struggle to articulate why a configuration worked. Encourage them to
point to the diagram while explaining.

Vocabulary: circuit, conductor, insulator, closed circuit, open circuit.

Assessment Opportunity: Completed works/doesn't-work chart with at least three configurations tried.

Existing Literacy Supports: A labeled diagram of a complete circuit is provided, but there is no
sentence frame or writing support for the explanation portion of the wrap-up.
